content.text: {"predictors": [{"name": "Supplier-Concentration Fragility", "construction": "Using 10-K disclosures and the Compustat Segment/Customer files, count the number of major suppliers a firm depends on and compute a Herfindahl index of purchase concentration when disclosed; where supplier detail is sparse, proxy using cost-of-goods-sold volatility (standard deviation of quarterly COGS/sales over trailing 12 quarters) as an inverse measure of supply diversification. Rank firms cross-sectionally each month.", "rationale": "Firms reliant on few suppliers bear un-diversified input-cost and disruption risk that is not fully priced, commanding a risk premium.", "higher_returns_for": "high supplier concentration / high COGS volatility"}, {"name": "Inventory-Mix Shift", "construction": "For manufacturers, decompose total inventory into raw materials, work-in-process, and finished goods from Compustat (INVRM, INVWIP, INVFG). Compute the year-over-year change in the finished-goods share of total inventory. Rank firms by this change each quarter after earnings.", "rationale": "A rising finished-goods share signals weakening demand and future markdowns not yet reflected in prices, predicting lower returns.", "higher_returns_for": "low (declining finished-goods share)"}, {"name": "Deferred Revenue Acceleration", "construction": "Using quarterly Compustat deferred revenue (current plus long-term), compute the second difference (acceleration) in deferred revenue scaled by lagged total assets over trailing four quarters. Rank cross-sectionally each quarter.", "rationale": "Accelerating deferred revenue reflects growing bookings of future obligations and recurring demand that the market underweights relative to reported earnings.", "higher_returns_for": "high deferred revenue acceleration"}, {"name": "Intra-Year Earnings Seasonality Strength", "construction": "For each firm, regress the last 20 quarters of seasonally-differenced earnings surprises and compute the autocorrelation of same-quarter-prior-year earnings growth. Form a score capturing how strongly a firm's same-calendar-quarter earnings tend to repeat. Buy stocks entering their historically strong quarter.", "rationale": "Predictable calendar-quarter earnings patterns are underreacted to by investors who anchor on recent quarters rather than seasonal analogs.", "higher_returns_for": "high seasonality score entering a historically strong quarter"}, {"name": "Capitalized R&D Vintage Skew", "construction": "Build an R&D capital stock using perpetual inventory (15% annual depreciation) from Compustat XRD, then compute the fraction of the stock originating in the most recent two fiscal years versus older vintages. Rank firms by the recent-vintage fraction.", "rationale": "Firms with young, fresh R&D pipelines have optionality and innovation not yet monetized, which the market values with a lag.", "higher_returns_for": "high recent-vintage fraction"}, {"name": "Dividend-Timing Consistency", "construction": "For dividend payers, compute the standard deviation of the calendar day-of-quarter on which dividends are declared and paid over the trailing 12 quarters using CRSP distribution dates. Lower dispersion means highly punctual payers. Rank firms by punctuality.", "rationale": "Managerial discipline in payout timing proxies for governance quality and cash-flow predictability, earning a modest premium mispriced by investors focused only on yield.", "higher_returns_for": "high timing consistency (low dispersion)"}, {"name": "Asset-Liquidation Value Gap", "construction": "Estimate liquidation value as cash + 0.75*receivables + 0.5*inventory + 0.5*net PP&E from Compustat, minus total liabilities. Scale by market cap to form a liquidation-to-price ratio. Rank cross-sectionally, focusing on the extreme high tail.", "rationale": "Stocks trading below tangible liquidation value carry a downside-protected deep-value premium under-arbitraged in small caps.", "higher_returns_for": "high liquidation-to-price ratio"}, {"name": "Short-Horizon Volume-Volatility Divergence", "construction": "Over the trailing 21 trading days, compute the correlation between daily dollar volume and daily absolute return using CRSP. A low or negative correlation indicates trading not driven by information. Rank firms by this correlation.", "rationale": "When volume decouples from volatility, trading is liquidity- or noise-driven, creating temporary mispricing that reverses, so low-divergence names outperform.", "higher_returns_for": "high volume-volatility correlation"}, {"name": "Tax-Loss Carryforward Utilization Momentum", "construction": "From Compustat and 10-K tax footnotes, track net operating loss carryforwards and compute the trailing-year decline in NOL balance as a share of pretax income (utilization rate). Rank firms by rising utilization.", "rationale": "Accelerating NOL utilization signals a durable return to profitability and shielded future cash flows that analysts capitalize slowly.", "higher_returns_for": "high NOL utilization momentum"}, {"name": "Geographic Revenue Dispersion", "construction": "Using Compustat geographic segment data, compute a Herfindahl index of revenue across reported geographic regions. Low concentration means geographically diversified revenue. Rank firms cross-sectionally by dispersion.", "rationale": "Geographically concentrated firms bear un-diversifiable regional macro risk that commands a premium, while the market underprices this exposure.", "higher_returns_for": "high geographic concentration (low dispersion)"}]}
